journey:denis-noli-me-tangere-reims.m: Oil on canvas (sketch for an arched composition, 54 × 150.5 cm)

x.summary: In a pale, wooded garden, the risen Christ stands before the kneeling Mary Magdalene and gestures to her not to approach, while showing her the wounds of his Passion. Around them Denis unfolds the rest of Easter morning: Peter and John hurrying to the tomb, and the holy women addressed by two angels guarding the sepulchre. The soft, luminous colours and arched format reflect Denis's lifelong ambition to renew sacred art for churches of the modern age.
facts: In 1919, the year before this painting, Denis co-founded the Ateliers d'Art Sacré in Paris with George Desvallières to train artists for the decoration of churches.

The lunette-shaped canvas, catalogued by the museum as a sketch (esquisse), relates to Denis's decoration of the chapel of the Prieuré, his home at Saint-Germain-en-Laye; it was bequeathed to Reims by the art historian and curator Paul Jamot in 1939.
Several episodes of the Resurrection appear side by side in the one landscape, a narrative device that recalls early Italian painting, which Denis deeply admired.
